title: Thus the Eternal Father Spake
description: Thus the Eternal Father Spake in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 110, part 1, headed “Christ exalted, and multitudes converted; or, The success of the gospel”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus the e-ter-nal Fa-ther spake To Christ the Son, "As-cend and sit "At my right hand, till I shall make "Thy foes sub-mis-sive at thy feet.

lines: To Christ the Son, "Ascend and sit
"At my right hand, till I shall make
"Thy word, the sceptre in thy hand,
"Shall make the hearts of rebels bleed,
"And bow their wills to thy command.
"That day shall shew thy power is great,
"When saints shall flock with willing minds,
What a large victory shall ensue!
And converts, who thy grace obey,
Exceed the drops of morning dew.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
